prompt: An Alabama Stage II (restricted) license holder generally may not drive during which hours?
options: 10 p.m. to 4 a.m.
9 p.m. to 5 a.m.
Midnight to 6 a.m.
There is no night restriction
explanation: A Stage II restricted driver may not drive between midnight and 6 a.m., except for work, school, religious, medical, or emergency reasons, or when accompanied by a licensed parent or guardian.

No passengers at all
No more than 1

prompt: In Alabama, a driver may obtain an unrestricted (Stage III) license when they are:
options: 17 and have held the Stage II license for at least 6 months
16 after completing driver education with no restricted-license period
18 regardless of how long the Stage II restricted license was held
16 after holding a learner license for at least 30 days
explanation: An Alabama driver can move to an unrestricted Stage III license at age 17, provided they have held the Stage II restricted license for at least 6 months with a clean record.

prompt: In Alabama, how many points accumulated within a 2-year period will trigger the first level of license suspension?
options: 20 points
12 points
8 points
6 points
explanation: Accumulating 12 to 14 points within 2 years results in a 60-day suspension in Alabama. Higher point totals lead to progressively longer suspensions, up to one year at 24 or more points.

Move over one lane away, or slow down if you cannot change lanes safely
Turn on your hazard lights and continue in the same lane at normal speed

A motorcycle-only endorsement added to a standard license
